name: Capella
description: Two yellow giants 13 parsecs away that circle each other every 104 days.

radius.source: Torres et al. (2015), ApJ 807, 26, Table 5: primary radius 11.98 +/- 0.57 solar radii

mass.source: Torres et al. (2015), ApJ 807, 26, Table 4: dynamical mass of the primary 2.5687 +/- 0.0074 solar masses

temperature.source: Torres et al. (2015), ApJ 807, 26, Table 5: primary Teff 4970 +/- 50 K

radialVelocity.source: Torres et al. (2015), ApJ 807, 26, Table 4: systemic velocity +29.9387 +/- 0.0032 km/s, on the frame of the Weber & Strassmeier (2011) velocities

distance.source: Torres et al. (2015), ApJ 807, 26, Table 4: distance 13.159 +/- 0.015 pc from the orbital parallax 75.994 +/- 0.089 mas

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

color.reason: Every spectrum of Capella is the blended light of both giants, and the secondary is the brighter in the Hipparcos band, (l_B/l_A)_Hp = 1.204 +/- 0.060 (Torres et al. 2015, ApJ 807, 26, Table 4), so no archive spectrum is the primary's own

text.card: Two yellow giants 13 parsecs away that circle each other every 104 days.
text.introduction: Its stars weigh 2.57 and 2.48 solar masses, from their orbit; the larger is 11.98 solar radii and 4,970 K at its surface.
